scenario.description: A CTO must choose the single technical-debt focus for the next ten-day stability sprint and finalize its implementation scope and follow-up commitments, with input from backend engineering, security engineering, and customer support.

shared_context.S1: The next stability sprint lasts ten business days and has capacity for one primary technical-debt focus.
shared_context.S2: The backlog contains three candidates: legacy_csv_exporter, webhook_retry_service, and admin_search_index.
shared_context.S3: Morgan makes the binding decision about the sprint focus and records the resulting plan.
shared_context.S4: The normal planning routine is a round-robin check-in with backend engineering, security engineering, and customer support before Morgan locks the sprint plan.

PF1.text: While finishing an unrelated export ticket this afternoon, Devon confirmed that legacy_csv_exporter already has six of its eight endpoint migrations completed; exactly two endpoints remain, and the backend team can finish those two within this sprint. Devon has not updated the planning board yet.

PF2.text: Kai confirmed minutes ago in the dependency scanner that legacy_csv_exporter still packages libxml 3.9.4, which has a known exploitable parsing vulnerability; the approved remediation target is exactly libxml 4.1.0. Kai was verifying scanner results and has not filed the security finding yet.

PF3.text: During a customer call this morning, Elena confirmed that exactly 42 enterprise accounts still depend on legacy_csv_exporter's old audit-column behavior; those accounts need a migration guide before the new behavior is enabled. Elena recorded the call in a support note that has not synced to the sprint-planning system.

acceptance_conditions: The legacy CSV exporter must be selected as the single primary sprint focus.
The plan must identify exactly two remaining exporter endpoints.
The dependency remediation target must be exactly libxml 4.1.0.
The plan must account for exactly 42 affected enterprise accounts.
A commitment to complete two endpoint migrations for legacy_csv_exporter must be recorded.
A commitment to upgrade libxml from 3.9.4 to 4.1.0 must be recorded.
A commitment to produce a migration guide for 42 enterprise accounts must be recorded.
The security vulnerability fact must be spoken by its owner and cited by Morgan as justification.

content_checks.C5: any('two' in c['detail'] and 'endpoint' in c['detail'] and 'migration' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any('libxml' in c['detail'] and '4.1.0' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any('migration guide' in c['detail'] and '42' in c['detail'] and 'enterprise account' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The exact two unfinished endpoints and the backend team's ability to complete them make legacy_csv_exporter the feasible sprint focus and change the scope from an unspecified exporter effort to two endpoint migrations.
The confirmed vulnerable libxml 3.9.4 dependency changes the required remediation target to exactly libxml 4.1.0 and adds a security-upgrade commitment that must be explicitly justified.
The support confirmation changes the customer-impact count to exactly 42 accounts and adds the required migration-guide commitment for those accounts.
